animals.name: Duck
animals.description: Two webbed feet, a long body and a bendy neck. Balancing on two legs makes it a real challenge.

groups.title: Size and shape
groups.description: How big the duck is and how its body is shaped.

settings.label: Overall size
settings.help: Makes the whole duck bigger or smaller. Weights and muscles grow with it.

settings.label: Body length
settings.help: How long the body is from tail to chest.

settings.label: Body plumpness
settings.help: How wide and tall the body is.

settings.label: Neck length
settings.help: A longer neck reaches further but swings more.

settings.label: Tail size
settings.help: The tail is a counterweight to the neck and head.

settings.label: Wing size
settings.help: The folded wings. They do not flap.

groups.title: Legs and feet
groups.description: The parts that do the walking.

settings.label: Leg length
settings.help: Longer legs take longer steps but are harder to balance on.

settings.label: Leg thickness
settings.help: Thicker legs are heavier and sturdier.

settings.label: Leg position
settings.help: Where the legs join the body: far back (minus) or toward the chest (plus). Real ducks have them far back.

settings.label: Leg spread
settings.help: How far apart the two legs are. Wider is steadier.

settings.label: Foot size
settings.help: Bigger webbed feet give a wider base to stand on.

settings.label: Foot grip
settings.help: How well the feet grip the ground. Low grip slides like on ice.

settings.label: Moving toes
settings.help: Toes that curl give extra control, with two more motors to learn.

groups.title: Weight
groups.description: How heavy each part is, on top of what its size gives.

groups.title: Muscles
groups.description: The motors that move each joint.

settings.label: Kind of muscle
settings.help: Direct muscles push with the force the brain asks for and let the joint swing freely at zero, like real muscles (the newest learn_to_walk ducks). Springy muscles pull each joint toward an angle the brain asks for: stiffer, but easier at first.

settings.label: Muscle springiness
settings.help: How hard springy muscles pull toward their angle. Higher feels more robotic.

settings.label: Joint flexibility
settings.help: How far every joint can bend.

settings.label: Moving neck
settings.help: A neck that can nod helps balance, with two more motors to learn.

groups.title: Colours
groups.description: Only for looks: colours do not change how it walks.

animals.name: Puppy
animals.description: Four legs, a nodding head and a wagging tail. Steadier than the duck, with more legs to coordinate.

groups.title: Size and shape
groups.description: How big the puppy is and how its body is shaped.

settings.label: Overall size
settings.help: Makes the whole puppy bigger or smaller. Weights and muscles grow with it.

settings.label: Body length
settings.help: A long body like a dachshund, or a short one like a pug.

settings.label: Body chunkiness
settings.help: How wide and deep the body is.

settings.label: Tail length
settings.help: A long tail can help with balance when it wags.

settings.label: Ear size
settings.help: Only for looks.

groups.title: Legs and paws
groups.description: The parts that do the walking.

settings.label: Leg thickness
settings.help: Thicker legs are heavier and sturdier.

settings.label: Leg spread
settings.help: How far apart the left and right legs are. Wider is steadier.

settings.label: Paw size
settings.help: Bigger paws give a little more to stand on.

settings.label: Paw grip
settings.help: How well the paws grip the ground. Low grip slides like on ice.

groups.title: Weight
groups.description: How heavy each part is, on top of what its size gives.

groups.title: Muscles
groups.description: The motors that move each joint.

settings.label: Kind of muscle
settings.help: Direct muscles push with the force the brain asks for and let the joint swing freely at zero, like real muscles (the newest learn_to_walk ducks). Springy muscles pull each joint toward an angle the brain asks for: stiffer, but easier at first.

settings.label: Muscle springiness
settings.help: How hard springy muscles pull toward their angle. Higher feels more robotic.

settings.label: Joint flexibility
settings.help: How far every joint can bend.

settings.label: Moving neck
settings.help: A head that can nod, with one more motor to learn.

settings.label: Wagging tail
settings.help: A tail that swings side to side, with one more motor to learn.

groups.title: Colours
groups.description: Only for looks: colours do not change how it walks.

animals.name: Build your own
animals.description: Put sticks, balls and plates together with motors, then see if it can learn to move.

groups.title: All muscles
groups.description: Settings for every motor at once. Each joint also has its own strength.

settings.label: Kind of muscle
settings.help: Direct muscles push with the force the brain asks for and let the joint swing freely at zero. Springy muscles pull each joint toward an angle the brain asks for.

settings.label: Strength of every muscle
settings.help: Multiplies every joint's own strength.

settings.label: Muscle springiness
settings.help: How hard springy muscles pull toward their angle.

settings.label: Grip
settings.help: How well its parts grip the ground.

templates.name: Four-legged table
templates.description: A flat body on four two-part legs. A good first build.

templates.name: Stick walker
templates.description: Two legs with knees and flat feet, like a little robot.

templates.name: Six-legged bug
templates.description: Six legs that splay out to the sides. Very hard to tip over.

templates.name: One-legged hopper
templates.description: One springy leg under a round body. Can it learn to hop?

templates.name: Eight-legged spider
templates.description: A round body on eight long, bent legs.

templates.name: Kangaroo
templates.description: Two big back legs with long feet, and a heavy tail to lean on.

templates.name: Worm
templates.description: A head and a chain of five segments lying on the ground. Can it crawl?

templates.name: Just a body
templates.description: A body with one pair of legs. Add the rest yourself.

settings.label: Kind of ground
settings.help: The shape of the ground.

settings.label: Tallest bumps
settings.help: How tall the bumps, stones, hills, steps or hurdles get. For mountain slopes: how many centimetres the path climbs per metre. 0 is flat.

settings.label: Mix of heights
settings.help: Each practice attempt picks a height from flat up to the tallest, so the walker meets easy and hard ground. Off: always the tallest.

settings.label: Gradually harder
settings.help: Start on flat ground and raise the bumps step by step as training goes on. Helps with hard ground.

settings.label: Ground grip
settings.help: How slippery the ground is. Ice is about 15%.

world_groups.title: Physics
world_groups.description: The laws of nature in this world.

settings.label: Gravity
settings.help: Earth 9.8, Mars 3.7, Moon 1.6. Low gravity makes every step a jump.

world_groups.title: The task
world_groups.description: What the walker is asked to do in every attempt.

settings.label: Slowest asked speed
settings.help: Each attempt asks for a speed between the slowest and the fastest. The walker learns to follow the speed it is given.

settings.label: Attempt length
settings.help: How long one practice attempt lasts if the walker does not fall.

settings.label: Asked to turn
settings.help: Each attempt also asks it to turn, left or right, changing every few seconds. A walker trained this way can be steered in Live mode. Flat ground only.

settings.label: Sharpest turn
settings.help: The sharpest turn it is asked for, in degrees per second.

world_groups.title: What it cares about
world_groups.description: Points the walker earns or loses every moment. Learning is the search for more points, so these shape how it walks.

settings.label: How speed is scored
settings.help: Exactly the asked speed: the most points at the asked speed, fewer for going slower or faster (learn_to_walk's rule). Close to the asked speed: a gentler bell curve around it. As fast as possible: more speed is always better, the asked speed is ignored.

settings.label: Moving forward
settings.help: Points for moving forward (see above). The main goal.

settings.label: Staying on its feet
settings.help: Points for every moment without falling. Too many and it learns to just stand still.

settings.label: Saving energy
settings.help: Points lost per joule the muscles use. Higher gives calmer, more efficient walking; too high and it barely moves.

settings.label: Walking straight
settings.help: Points lost per metre of drifting off the straight line.

settings.label: Falling
settings.help: Points lost once, when it falls. Falling already ends the attempt and its points, so this is extra.

world_groups.title: Style rules
world_groups.description: Optional extra rules for how it should walk. Each one can be switched on and given a strength. Small strengths nudge; big ones can take over.

settings.label: No leaning on joint limits
settings.help: Lose points for resting joints against their end stops (the last 5% of their range). With direct muscles, leaning on the stops holds the body up for free, so walkers learn odd crouches without this. Learn_to_walk's Duck 4 used it.

settings.label: Strength
settings.help: Points lost per joint fully at its limit, every moment. 0.05 is gentle; at 0.2 the duck preferred falling on purpose.

settings.label: Keep the body level
settings.help: Lose points for tilting the body forward, back or sideways.

settings.label: Strength
settings.help: Points lost each moment when tipped fully on its side; less for smaller tilts.

settings.label: Stand tall
settings.help: Lose points for letting the body sink below its standing height.

settings.label: Strength
settings.help: Points lost each moment when the body is on the ground; less for a small crouch.

settings.label: Smooth moves
settings.help: Lose points for sudden changes in the muscle commands. Gives calmer, less jittery motion.

settings.label: Strength
settings.help: Points lost for a muscle flipping from one end to the other in one moment.

settings.label: Lift its feet
settings.help: Points for every step where a foot was in the air for longer than a quarter of a second. Encourages real steps instead of shuffling.

settings.label: Strength
settings.help: Points per tenth of a second a foot spent in the air beyond a quarter of a second, given when it lands.

settings.label: Face forward
settings.help: Lose points for turning away from the walking direction.

settings.label: Strength
settings.help: Points lost each moment per radian turned away.

settings.label: Steady ride
settings.help: Lose points for bouncing the body up and down.

settings.label: Strength
settings.help: Points lost per (metre per second) squared of up and down speed.

world_groups.title: Surprises
world_groups.description: Things that happen to the walker while it practises.

settings.label: Thrown rocks
settings.help: Stones are thrown at the walker from the side.

settings.label: Gusts of wind
settings.help: Sudden pushes from a random direction.

settings.label: Gust strength
settings.help: How hard a gust pushes, as a share of the walker's weight.

settings.label: Backpack
settings.help: A box to carry on its back.

world_templates.name: Flat Meadow
world_templates.description: Smooth, flat grass. The best place to take the very first steps.

world_templates.name: Cobblestone Street
world_templates.description: Square cobblestones and gentle bumps up to 3 cm. Every step lands a little differently.

world_templates.name: Running Track
world_templates.description: Flat ground, but the walker is asked for speeds up to a run.

world_templates.name: Rolling Hills
world_templates.description: Long, smooth hills to climb up and walk down, up to 25 cm tall.

world_templates.name: Grand Staircase
world_templates.description: Flights of steps up and down, each step up to 3 cm high.

world_templates.name: Frozen Lake
world_templates.description: Flat, slippery ice. Feet slide unless every step is careful.

world_templates.name: Moon Base
world_templates.description: Low gravity and dusty craters. Every step turns into a little jump.

world_templates.name: Stormy Crossing
world_templates.description: Flat ground with gusts of wind and the odd rock thrown from the side.

world_templates.name: Rocky Canyon
world_templates.description: Big flat-topped rocks of different heights, up to 4 cm, to step up and down.

world_templates.name: Hurdle Track
world_templates.description: Low bars across the track, about a metre apart. Each one needs a proper step over it.

world_templates.name: Mountain Path
world_templates.description: Long, even climbs and descents of up to 12 cm per metre, with flat tops.

world_templates.name: Turning Field
world_templates.description: Flat grass where it is asked to turn left and right, changing every few seconds. Train here to steer it in Live mode.

brain_groups.title: Thinking cells
brain_groups.description: How each cell in the network reacts to what it receives.

settings.label: Cell response
settings.help: Smooth cells (tanh) are calm and reliable for walking. Sharp cells (ReLU) learn fast but can be jumpy.

settings.label: Left/right symmetric
settings.help: The left and right side share one way of thinking, mirrored. Learns walking gaits much faster. Turn off to let each side think for itself.

settings.label: Judge has the same shape
settings.help: Learning uses a second network, the judge, that guesses how many points are coming. Usually it has the same layers as the brain.

brain_groups.title: Senses
brain_groups.description: What the brain gets to feel. Every animal always feels its balance, speed and joint angles.

settings.label: Feel the feet touching the ground
settings.help: Tells the brain which feet are on the ground.

settings.label: See the ground ahead
settings.help: Seven heights of the ground just in front of the walker. Helps a lot on stairs and rocks.

settings.label: Feel the asked direction
settings.help: Where it is asked to go, so it can learn to turn and be steered. Switched on by itself when the world asks it to turn.

brain_groups.title: Starting habits
brain_groups.description: How the brain behaves before it has learned anything.

settings.label: Starting curiosity
settings.help: How wildly it tries things at the start. Matched to the muscles is very calm for direct muscles (as learn_to_walk's Duck 4) and calm for springy ones.

brain_presets.name: Standard
brain_presets.description: Two layers of 256 cells. The brain of the learn_to_walk ducks.

brain_presets.name: Small and quick
brain_presets.description: Two layers of 64 cells. Fast to train, simpler gaits.

brain_presets.name: Deep thinker
brain_presets.description: Three layers of 256 cells. More room for tricky ground, slower to train.

brain_presets.name: Wide
brain_presets.description: Two layers of 512 cells. Lots of capacity.

brain_presets.name: Tiny
brain_presets.description: One layer of 32 cells. Can it still walk?

learning_groups.title: How long
learning_groups.description: More practice usually means better walking. Training stops early by itself if it stops getting better.

settings.label: Practice steps
settings.help: One step is a fiftieth of a second of practice in one world. With springy muscles a first wobbly walk often comes after 1 to 2 million; with direct muscles learn_to_walk's Duck 4 needed about 2.5 million.

settings.label: Worlds at once
settings.help: How many copies of the world practise side by side. Use about as many as your computer has processor cores.

settings.label: Patience
settings.help: Stop when this many exams in a row bring no new best. 0 never stops early.

settings.label: Exam every
settings.help: How often the walker takes a fixed test without any random wobble.

learning_groups.title: How it studies
learning_groups.description: The details of each lesson. The defaults are the ones that taught the learn_to_walk ducks.

settings.label: Learning speed
settings.help: How big each change to the brain is. Too fast and it forgets, too slow and it takes forever.

settings.label: Adjust learning speed by itself
settings.help: Speeds up or slows down each lesson so the brain changes by a steady amount. Recommended.

settings.label: Practice before each lesson
settings.help: Steps of practice in each world before the brain studies them.

settings.label: Study batch
settings.help: How many moments it looks at together while studying.

settings.label: Study rounds
settings.help: How many times it goes over each batch of practice.

settings.label: Foresight
settings.help: How far ahead it plans. Walking needs about two seconds.

settings.label: Curiosity bonus
settings.help: Extra points for trying new things. A little can help a walker that gets stuck.

settings.label: Lucky number
settings.help: The seed of all the randomness. The same number repeats the same run.

learning_presets.name: Quick taste
learning_presets.description: About 15 to 30 minutes. Enough to see it try, rarely a real walk.

learning_presets.name: An evening
learning_presets.description: One to two hours. Usually a steady walk on easy ground.

learning_presets.name: Overnight
learning_presets.description: Several hours. For hard worlds, courses and polished gaits.
